newsitem.title: FRANCE: Castorama up on outlook, broker upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Castorama up on outlook, broker upgrade.

text.p: Shares in French home improvements chain Castorama climbed on Tuesday in heavy volume on hopes for favourable results in the coming years and news it would proceed with its plan to buy 100 percent of Canadian chain Reno Depot.

French broker SGE Delahaye raised its recommendation on Castorama shares to "buy" from "neutral", despite the announcement late on Monday of a 1.6 percent rise in 1996 net profit, which was judged disappointing by several analysts.

Castorama shares were up 3.75 percent at 913 francs at 1123 GMT after hitting a high of 930 earlier on Tuesday with a volume of 154,545 shares. The CAC-40 index of blue-chip stocks was up 0.53 percent.

Delahaye analyst Liliane Dufroid-Reynaud said she decided to upgrade Castorama because the shares did not look expensive taking into account the favourable outlook for 1998. However she said the surge in the share price was "a little strong".

She said she expected 1997 to be another year of investment and transition and that the results for the year would not be "exceptional". She was also awaiting further details about the acquisition of Reno Depot.
Credit Commercial de France, however, was said to have lowered its recommendation to "lighten" from "buy", markets sources said. No confirmation from CCF was immediately available.
